newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bares fangs of military attack dog unit.
newsitem.headline: Israel bares fangs of military attack dog unit.

text.p: Israel's state television on Friday took the wraps off a military unit whose members are trained to fight Arab guerrillas with their bare teeth: the army general staff's attack dog force.
"They are savage dogs, trained for one purpose: to bite and not let go," the television said.

It said the dozens of attack dogs, working with crack soldiers, were deployed primarily along the borders with the West Bank and Gaza, outside areas of Palestinian self-rule, and on Israel's northern border with Lebanon.
The dogs are trained to locate guerrilla infiltrators, it said, and "'to neutralise them', the delicate military term meaning to assault the subject and sink teeth into one of his body parts."
"The prize is the bite -- they really love to bite," said First Sergeant Amiad Daniel, commader of one of the units. "That's what boosts their motivation to work."

With heavily padded soldiers posing as guerrillas in Arab garb, the television showed Rottweilers, German and Belgian Shepherds, Dobermans and other breeds trained to track and bring down "terrorist suspects" -- with a visegrip on the forearm.
It showed the dogs, some helicopter-borne, were also trained to strip guerrillas of their weapons, and to enter occupied buildings that posed a deadly risk to soldiers.
The army has long been reticent about acknowledging the existence of a canine corps, except in such roles as rescue work or in sniffing out explosives.

In the past some Israelis have voiced reservations over the army's use of dogs in attack roles, saying they evoked memories of the animals employed by German troops during the World War Two Nazi Holocaust, in which six million Jews were killed.
